answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with reputation-weighted transaction caps: every new identity starts near zero, able to handle only trivial trades, and its cap rises slowly as completed work is attested by independent counterparties over time. Like a meadow that grows back slowly after grazing, trust regrows at a fixed pace no matter how many identities an attacker plants. On the horizon, a fake identity's lifetime value stays below the cost of building its history, and each clone falls off the same ledge of starting from zero — so mass-producing identities buys nothing.
